title: Prefix compacting: hit-rate sensitivity analysis, TTL safety knobs, and cache-key hygiene playbook
creator: Marcus Alvarez
description: Run a targeted set of experiments and produce an operational playbook for safely applying prefix compacting and TTL adjustments. Focus on hit-rate sensitivity to key reshaping (compacting), small TTL deltas, and automated rollback triggers to protect cost and latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible notebook that estimates hit-rate delta from prefix compacting for a representative 10% traffic sample
A set of TTL safety knobs (max delta, per-prefix confidence interval) encoded as config parameters in the orchestration layer
Canary pipeline that applies compacting + TTL changes to <1% traffic and includes automated rollback on defined signal degradation
Playbook document with step-by-step safe-apply checklist, monitoring queries, and postmortem templates
Unit/integration tests for config validator (rejects >X% TTL shrink without confidence) merged to repo
design_decisions: Prefer prefix compacting (join/squash low-cardinality affixes) over global TTL shrink for initial rollout because it localizes risk to a subset of keys
Use bootstrap sampling to compute per-prefix hit elasticity rather than global heuristics — improves downstream cost estimates for tail prefixes
Expose two safety knobs: 'max_ttl_delta_pct' and 'min_confidence_z' in the rollout config; both are enforced by the config validator
Rollback thresholds use a composite signal: 5-minute rolling increase in backend miss rate + 99th percentile latency regression > 20% triggers auto-revert
Keep compacting changes idempotent and reversible by tracking canonicalization mapping in change metadata
experiments: Experiment A: Sampled offline simulation using 30 days of prefix logs to measure hit elasticity when merging top-1000 low-entropy affixes; notebook 'compact-sim-v1.ipynb'
Experiment B: Live shadow canary that applies compacting to 0.5% traffic and records delta on cache hit/miss, token cost, and tail latency over 48 hours
Experiment C: TTL micro-adjustments — run +10%, -10% TTL deltas per prefix cohort and model hit-rate response curve (spline fit) to estimate marginal benefit
Experiment D: Stress test under bursty request mix (synthetic workload) to ensure compacting does not create hot key amplification
Primary metric: cost-per-1000-tokens (estimate) and percentage change in global KV hit-rate; secondary: p99 latency, error rate
rollout_plan: Step 0: Run offline sample sim and produce per-prefix elasticity estimates with 95% CI
Step 1: Create change bundle with (a) prefix compacting rules, (b) TTL delta per-prefix, (c) safety knobs set to conservative defaults
Step 2: Deploy to stage environment and run full integration tests (config validator, canary harness) — 24h
Step 3: Canary live to 0.5% traffic for 48h. Monitor composite rollback signals. If safe, expand to 5% for 24h, then 20% for 24h, then full lane with gradual ramp
Step 4: Automated rollback: if composite signal tripped, the orchestrator reverts TTL and compacting rules and notifies on-call with runbook link
Step 5: Post-apply review after 7 days: collect cost delta, quality regression (where applicable), perf regressions, and update playbook
monitoring: Dashboard tiles: per-prefix hit-rate, cache miss-to-backend ratio, per-prefix RPS, p50/p95/p99 tail latencies
Derived signals: 'hit_elasticity' (delta hit-rate / delta-keys) and 'cost_estimated_delta' computed from token mix and hit elasticity
Alerting rules: critical if miss-rate increases by >10% for 5m and p99 latency > 20% of baseline
SLO probes: synthetic user-facing flows exercising affected prefixes every 10m to capture end-to-end regressions
Observability artifacts: link to cost dashboard, tracing spans for cache lookup path, histogram snapshots pre/post apply
risks: Hot-key amplification if compacting inadvertently merges a high-frequency suffix with others; mitigated by excluding high-RPS prefixes from compaction candidate set
Underestimated downstream cost if token mix shifts after TTL changes — mitigation: short canaries and conservative initial TTL deltas
False confidence from small-sample CI when traffic distribution is seasonal — require sampling across multiple windows (peak vs off-peak)
Operational complexity: compaction mapping must be stored and versioned to support reversible changes; forgetting this leads to unrecoverable divergence
Client-side assumptions: SDKs that rely on stable cache-key shapes may break if compaction changes canonicalization — need a compatibility guide
dependencies: Console: create new dashboard tiles (Console-357) for per-prefix metrics
